cumleler: When chemotherapy ends, does the risk of hearing loss end too?
Cisplatin is a platinum-based chemotherapy drug used for many solid tumors.
It damages basal outer hair cells, so loss starts at high frequencies.
Loss is reported in about half or more of treated children.
The drug can remain in cochlear tissue for months, even years.
So loss can progress after treatment ends; monitoring continues.
